items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: a trombone teacher, John Coffey from Boston, was a wonderful friend and a great teacher

ctx.x: Did you have teacher aspirations as a high school student and so forth, or did you have professional music aspirations, or was it just a combination of both?

It wasn’t a combination of both. I really wanted to be a professional musician. I didn’t think about education until I was in the service during World War II, and when I got back from the service I got married and began to raise a family, and actually a trombone teacher, John Coffey from Boston, was a wonderful friend and a great teacher, and took an interest in all of his students personally. It was John that said to me, you know, “Why don’t you consider going into education, since you’re raising a family?” I…
That’s good to hear because sometimes teachers are often frustrated I think.
